newsitem.title: UK: India news fails to stir Europe veg oil trade.
newsitem.headline: India news fails to stir Europe veg oil trade.

text.p: European vegetable oil traders expressed little surprise on Wednesday at news that India is likely to scale down imports of palm oil in coming months.
"People have been expecting this so it isn't a factor," said one trader.

India, one of the world's largest edible oil importers, is expect to reduce purchases over the coming months following a good oilseed crop harvest and adequate palm olein stocks, according to local industry officals.

India imported around 80,000 to 100,000 tonnes of palm olein month during September, October and November, but this could be reduced to around 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes a month for the next three to four months.
"Noone is surpised by this news and people are more focused on the soyoil and China situation," said another trader.
Traders said palm oil was looking over-priced against soy oil and this along with talk of lower Chinese buying of palm oil then expected was begining to affect sentiment.

"People were talking in terms of China buying 100,000 tonnes of palm oil a month during November and December but now it's looking more like it's going to be around 70,000 to 75,000 tonnes, which is a low figure," said one trader.
Some traders said China had been buying more soyoil than expected while others noted that China normally reduces its intake of palm oil during the winter.
"What ever way you look at the market at the moment there isn't any bullish news," said a trader.
Prices over the past week have hardly moved with soy oil and rape oil 0.50 guilders up and crude palm oil $5 down to $5 up.

Slow shipments of coconut oil from origin are keeping nearby months firm, but with around five vessels due this week the over all gain in the past week as been reduced to $5 while forward positions are $15 down.
Palmkernel oil is $5 up to $10 down over the week.
A lack of rapeseed sellers and concern over modified soybeans has kept rape oil at a perimum of three to five guilders over soy oil.
On Wednesday morning soy oil opened one to 1.25 guilders down and rape oil one to 1.50 guilders lower following the easier close in Chicago
Based on sellers' prices, the premium for rape oil over soy oil was 4.50 to 5.50 guilders at the opening against 2.50 to six guilders at Tuesday's close.
Opening crude palm oil sellers were unchanged to $2.50 up after Dec traded at $547.50 a tonne.
In early trading palm olein fetched $552.50 for Dec and $547.50 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for Jan/Mar.
Lauric oils were not quoted at the opening.
